exercises.title: Chest tummy time
exercises.benefit: Builds neck strength in the safest, cosiest spot — on you.
steps: Recline at ~45° and lay {name} tummy-down on your chest
Talk softly — your voice invites the head to lift
Start with 1–2 minutes, a few times a day
exercises.stop_signs: Stop if baby fully falls asleep in this position — move to the crib on the back.

exercises.title: Finger grasp play
exercises.benefit: Feeds the grasp reflex that becomes voluntary holding.
steps: Stroke {name}'s palm with your finger
Let the little fist close around it
Gently tug — feel the grip resist — release and repeat on the other hand
exercises.stop_signs: Stop if hands stay tightly fisted and baby gets upset — try after a feed.

exercises.title: Face tracking
exercises.benefit: Trains eye muscles and early focus — your face is the best target.
steps: Hold {name} 8–12 inches from your face during calm alert time
Slowly move your face side to side
Wait for the eyes to catch up — they may lag or cross at first, that's typical
exercises.stop_signs: Stop when baby looks away or fusses — that's the full-tank signal.

exercises.title: Bicycle legs
exercises.benefit: Eases gas and works the hips — the classic for a reason.
steps: Lay baby on the back on a firm surface
Hold the shins and cycle the legs gently, one at a time
Add a slow both-knees-to-tummy press, hold 3 seconds, release
exercises.stop_signs: Stop if any movement seems to cause pain (crying that spikes with the motion).

exercises.title: Side-lying play
exercises.benefit: A gentle strength position that also gives the head a break from lying flat.
steps: Lay {name} on one side on the floor, a rolled towel behind the back for support
Place your face or a high-contrast card in view
Switch sides halfway — awake and supervised only
exercises.stop_signs: Stop and place on the back if baby starts to doze — sleep is always on the back.

exercises.title: Classic floor tummy time
exercises.benefit: The main strength program: neck, shoulders, core.
steps: Firm blanket on the floor, baby tummy-down
Get down to eye level — your face is the motivation
Short and frequent beats long and tearful: build toward 3–5 minutes
exercises.stop_signs: Stop before frustration boils over; a few grumbles are fine, distress is not.

exercises.title: High-contrast tracking
exercises.benefit: Sharpens visual focus with the patterns young eyes see best.
steps: Hold a black-and-white card 8–12 inches away
Move it slowly in a shallow arc
Follow the eyes — pause when they lock on, then continue
exercises.stop_signs: Stop when gaze drifts away repeatedly — session's over.

exercises.title: Sound turning
exercises.benefit: Connects hearing and head control — early localization practice.
steps: During alert time, shake a soft rattle out of view to one side
Give {name} time to turn toward the sound
Reward the turn with your face and a cheer; alternate sides
exercises.stop_signs: Stop if there's never any reaction to sounds across days — mention it at the next checkup.

exercises.title: Hands to midline
exercises.benefit: Bringing hands together at the chest wires the two body halves to cooperate.
steps: With baby on the back, place a light toy on the chest
Guide both hands to touch it together
Let go and see if the hands stay — clapping games help too
exercises.stop_signs: Stop if one side consistently doesn't join in — worth mentioning to your pediatrician.

exercises.title: Mirror time
exercises.benefit: Self-discovery and face study — babies are their own favorite show.
steps: Prop a baby-safe mirror at floor level during tummy time
Let {name} study the reflection
Name what they see: 'That's you! Those are your eyes'
exercises.stop_signs: Standard tummy-time limits apply — end before the meltdown.

exercises.title: Sing and reply
exercises.benefit: Serve-and-return: the core drill of language and social wiring.
steps: Sing a short simple song with exaggerated expressions
Pause — leave space for {name} to answer with coos
Echo their sound back, then continue the song
exercises.stop_signs: No stop signs — this one only ends when one of you is done smiling.

exercises.title: Reach for the toy
exercises.benefit: Turns swipes into aimed reaches — the bridge to grabbing.
steps: Dangle a bright toy just within arm's reach during back play
Wiggle it until the eyes lock on
Wait for the reach — don't rush to hand it over; the effort is the exercise
exercises.stop_signs: Stop at frustration point — success should come at least sometimes; move the toy closer.

exercises.title: Tummy pivot play
steps: During tummy time, place a toy to the side just out of reach
Let {name} work to turn the body toward it
Move the toy in a slow circle over sessions — both directions
exercises.stop_signs: End before exhaustion — pivoting is heavy work.

exercises.title: Supported sitting
exercises.benefit: Builds trunk control with you as the safety frame.
steps: Sit baby between your legs on the floor, your hands at the ribs
Loosen support gradually as the back firms up
Cushion the sides — wobbles and tips are the learning
exercises.stop_signs: Stop if the head consistently flops — more neck time first, sitting later.

exercises.title: Grab and transfer
exercises.benefit: Practices passing objects hand to hand — coordination milestone prep.
steps: Offer a light ring toy to one hand
Once held, offer your finger to the same hand — watch the toy switch hands to grab you
Repeat starting from the other hand
exercises.stop_signs: No pressure version: if transfer doesn't happen yet, just enjoy the grabbing.

exercises.title: Rolling runway
exercises.benefit: Sets up the environment where the first roll can happen safely.
steps: Clear floor zone, baby on the back
Hold a toy above the chest, then move it slowly to one side at floor level
Let the eyes, then shoulders, then hips follow — assist the last bit with a gentle hip guide if baby strains
exercises.stop_signs: Never leave mid-session — this is exactly the practice that produces surprise rolls.
